issues.title: fix(physics): Investigate Case 600 series peak_heating under-prediction (610, 630, 640)
issues.body:
## Problem Statement

Cases 610, 630, and 640 show systematic peak_heating under-prediction while simultaneously showing peak_cooling over-prediction. This bidirectional error is the signature of a discrete-node solar-injection pathology documented in KNOWN_ISSUES.md LIMIT-05.

| Case | Metric | Fluxion | Reference Band | Deviation |
|------|--------|---------|----------------|----------|
| 610 | peak_heating | 3.26 kW | 4.30–5.70 kW | −24.2% UNDER |
| 630 | peak_heating | 3.16 kW | 4.70–6.10 kW | −32.8% UNDER |
| 640 | peak_heating | 3.13 kW | 4.30–5.70 kW | −27.2% UNDER |

**Source**: `docs/ASHRAE140_RESULTS.md` (2026-07-31 snapshot)

## Evidence
- Test: `cargo test --test ashrae_140_case_600_series`
- KNOWN_ISSUES.md §LIMIT-05 UPDATE (post-#1457 revisit) documents the 14 remaining failures
- `tests/known_issues_regression.rs::issue_1457_case_600_series_tracking` reproduces all 14 metrics

## Impact

These failures block improvement of the ASHRAE 140 pass rate from the current 18.8%. The 5R1C model architectural limitation is documented but the exact mathematical root cause in the solar-injection / timestep integration needs further investigation.

## Root Cause Hypothesis

Per LIMIT-05 UPDATE, the simultaneous peak_heating UNDER + peak_cooling OVER pattern cannot be fixed by adjusting thermal mass constants — it requires either:
1. Sub-hour air-node sub-stepping (reduces dt/τ from ~3.6 to manageable values)
2. GaugeSolver rework (#1465) treating solar as geometric curvature rather than per-timestep energy injection

The KNOWN_ISSUES.md states: _"The correct fix is the GaugeSolver (#1465 / #1462), which treats solar as geometric curvature rather than per-timestep energy injection."_

## Suggested Approach

1. **Immediate**: Verify that `solar_distribution_to_air = 0.7` is being applied correctly in the 5R1C path for the Case 600 series geometry
2. **Short-term**: Investigate whether the 1-hour timestep with dt/τ ≈ 3.6 is causing the discrete-node pathology documented in LIMIT-05
3. **Long-term**: Accelerate GaugeSolver Phase 3 (#1465) which is the architectural fix for this class of issue

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Cases 610, 630, 640 peak_heating within ±15% of reference band midpoint
- [ ] No regression in Cases 600, 620, 650 peak_heating (currently within band)
- [ ] `cargo test --test ashrae_140_case_600_series` shows improved pass rate
- [ ] Root cause documented in a follow-up issue with specific mathematical analysis

issues.title: fix(physics): Investigate Case 650 night ventilation ineffectiveness (SOLAR-04)
issues.body:
## Problem Statement

Case 650 (low-mass night ventilation) and Case 950 (high-mass night ventilation) show minimal cooling reduction from night ventilation. Reference programs show significant cooling reduction, but Fluxion shows nearly identical energy to non-ventilated cases (600/900).

**KNOWN_ISSUES.md SOLAR-04**: _"Case 650 (low-mass night ventilation) and Case 950 (high-mass night ventilation) test the effectiveness of nighttime natural ventilation for reducing daytime cooling. Reference shows significant cooling reduction. Fluxion shows minimal effect."_

## Evidence

From `docs/ASHRAE140_RESULTS.md`:
| Case | Annual Cooling | Reference | Status |
|------|--------------|----------|--------|
| 650 | 4430.34 kWh | 4820–7060 kWh | −10% UNDER |
| 950 | 105439.29 kWh | 390–920 kWh | **+11400% OVER** |

Case 650 is under-predicting cooling (night ventilation not helping), while Case 950 is massively over-predicting.

## Impact

SOLAR-04 is an open issue affecting two case series. Night ventilation is a key ASHRAE 140 test case for passive cooling strategies.

## Root Cause Hypothesis

Per KNOWN_ISSUES.md: _"Night ventilation parameter exists in case specs but may not be correctly applied in ventilation heat transfer calculations. Infiltration/ventilation rate multiplication during night hours needs verification."_

The ventilation rate may not be getting multiplied during the night hours (22:00–07:00) as specified in the ASHRAE 140 case definitions.

## Suggested Approach

1. Verify `NightVentilation` struct in `fluxion-core/src/ashrae_cases.rs` is being read correctly
2. Trace the night ventilation rate through `VentilationSchedule::get_ach()` for night hours
3. Check if the ACH multiplication is happening in `step_physics` for the ventilation path
4. Compare with ASHRAE 140 Table 1-12N specification for night ventilation rates

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Case 650 annual cooling within ±15% of reference midpoint (4820–7060 kWh)
- [ ] Case 950 annual cooling within ±50% of reference midpoint (390–920 kWh) — noting Case 950 has multiple issues
- [ ] Night ventilation ACH is applied during 22:00–07:00 hours in the simulation
- [ ] Test added to verify night ventilation rate multiplication

issues.title: feat(validation): Populate HVAC BESTEST validation scaffold (Issue #1754)
issues.body:
## Problem Statement

`tests/validation/hvac_bestest/mod.rs` exists as an empty scaffold (Issue #1754). The HVAC BESTEST RP-865 validation track has no case definitions, reference bounds, or acceptance tolerances.

**ARCHITECTURE.md §HVAC BESTEST validation scaffold (#1754)**:
> `tests/validation/hvac_bestest/mod.rs` is the integration-test root for the RP-865-derived HVAC BESTEST track. The initial target is intentionally empty and runs with `cargo test --test hvac_bestest`; follow-on issues own all case definitions, reference bounds, and acceptance tolerances.

## Evidence

- File: `tests/validation/hvac_bestest/mod.rs`
- Status: Empty scaffold, no test cases defined
- Command: `cargo test --test hvac_bestest` runs but has no cases

## Impact

HVAC BESTEST is a key validation suite for HVAC system modeling. Without it, there's no validation path for:
- VAV terminal units (#1764)
- DOAS units (#1765)
- Part-load curves (#1766)
- Airside coupling (#1767)

## Suggested Approach

1. **Phase 1**: Define 3-5 analytical BESTEST cases (no reference data needed):
   - Case E100: Constant volume air handler, heating only
   - Case E200: Constant volume air handler, cooling only  
   - Case E300: VAV system with reheat
   
2. **Phase 2**: Add comparative cases with EnergyPlus reference data
   - Case E400: VAV vs EnergyPlus VAV
   - Case E500: DOAS vs EnergyPlus DOAS

3. **Reference bounds**: Use ASHRAE RP-865 methodology for tolerance bands (±10% for annual energy, ±15% for peak loads)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `cargo test --test hvac_bestest` runs with at least 3 defined cases
- [ ] Each case has documented reference bounds and tolerance
- [ ] At least one case covers VAV terminal unit (#1764)
- [ ] Integration test harness follows same pattern as `ashrae_140_case_600_series`

issues.title: feat(interop): Complete IDF → SimulationSchema conversion (Issue #1341 follow-up)
issues.body:
## Problem Statement

The IDF import scaffold landed in #1341 (`src/io/idf/`), but the `TryFrom<IdfFile> for SimulationSchema` conversion is still pending (design §4.3 in `docs/idf-import-design.md`).

**ARCHITECTURE.md**: _"IDF import scaffold landed in `src/io/idf/` (#1341) covering the 10 MVP objects from design §4.1 — `TryFrom<IdfFile> for SimulationSchema` (design §4.3) and epJSON parsing (design §4.2) are still follow-up issues."_

## Evidence

- File: `src/io/idf/mod.rs` — lexer + parser scaffold
- Missing: `SimulationSchema` conversion from `IdfFile`
- Missing: epJSON parsing

## Impact

Without IDF import, users cannot:
- Import existing EnergyPlus models into Fluxion
- Validate Fluxion against EnergyPlus reference models
- Use Fluxion in workflows that start from EnergyPlus

This is a key interop gap blocking adoption.

## Suggested Approach

1. **Implement `TryFrom<IdfFile> for SimulationSchema`**:
   - Map the 10 MVP objects (Building, ThermalZone, Material, Construction, Schedule, etc.) to `SimulationSchema` types
   - Follow the type mapping defined in `docs/idf-import-design.md` §4.3

2. **Implement epJSON parsing**:
   - Add `FromStr` implementation for `IdfFile` supporting epJSON format
   - Reuse lexer/tokenizer from the IDF parser

3. **Add round-trip tests**:
   - Import an IDF file
   - Export via OSM module
   - Verify key fields are preserved

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `IdfFile` can be parsed from both IDF and epJSON formats
- [ ] `TryFrom<IdfFile> for SimulationSchema` converts the 10 MVP object types
- [ ] Round-trip test: IDF → SimulationSchema → IDF preserves key fields
- [ ] At least one ASHRAE 140 case IDF model can be imported

issues.title: feat(gauge-solver): Complete Phase 3 - Case 900 annual energy validation (Issue #1465)
issues.body:
## Problem Statement

GaugeSolver Phase 3 validation harness (`tests/gauge_validation_case_900.rs`) uses a **synthetic analytical CSV** rather than real EnergyPlus hourly data. The Phase 3 acceptance criteria require CSV reference parity but the current CSV is computed from the gauge solver formula, not from EnergyPlus.

**ARCHITECTURE.md §Phase 3 validation harness (issue #1465)**:
> The CSV at `tests/reference_data/gauge/case_900_diurnal_reference.csv` is **synthetic / analytical**, computed from the documented `GaugeSolver` formula.

> When a real EnergyPlus hourly Case 900 CSV becomes available (the existing annual-aggregate reference is not hourly), replace the synthetic fixture.

## Evidence

- File: `tests/reference_data/gauge/case_900_diurnal_reference.csv`
- Status: Synthetic, not from EnergyPlus
- Issue: Annual ±15% Case 900 energy tolerance tests are `#[ignore]` pending this

## Impact

The GaugeSolver Phase 3 validation cannot confirm that the gauge-theoretic approach matches EnergyPlus on annual energy basis. This is the key validation milestone for the gauge-theory research program (#1461, #1462, #1464).

## Suggested Approach

1. **Generate EnergyPlus hourly reference**:
   - Use `tests/reference_data/energyplus_models/ashrae_140_case_900.idf`
   - Run EnergyPlus 25.2.0 with the Denver TMY3 weather
   - Export hourly zone temperature, heating load, cooling load

2. **Replace synthetic CSV**:
   - Update `case_900_diurnal_reference.csv` with E+ hourly data
   - Update `tests/gauge_validation_case_900.rs` to use the real data

3. **Enable ignored tests**:
   - Remove `#[ignore]` from `test_case_900_annual_energy_within_15_percent`
   - Run against the new reference data

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `case_900_diurnal_reference.csv` contains EnergyPlus-generated hourly data (not synthetic)
- [ ] `tests/gauge_validation_case_900.rs` validates diurnal swing + phase lag against real E+ data
- [ ] Annual heating/cooling energy within ±15% of E+ reference
- [ ] `#[ignore]` attribute removed from annual energy tests

issues.title: fix(physics): Investigate ventilation_airflow TODO in physics_impl.rs
issues.body:
## Problem Statement

Two TODO comments in `src/sim/thermal_model_physics/physics_impl.rs` indicate that `ventilation_airflow` is hardcoded to a placeholder value instead of being read from the building specification:

```rust
// Line 927:
10000.0, // TODO: ventilation_airflow from building spec (m³/s)

// Line 3300:
10000.0, // TODO: ventilation_airflow from building spec (m³/s)
```

This means ventilation is not correctly coupling to the building specification, which would affect all cases.

## Evidence

- Files: `src/sim/thermal_model_physics/physics_impl.rs` lines 927, 3300
- Hardcoded value: `10000.0` m³/s (unrealistic — typical office is ~0.1–0.5 m³/s)

## Impact

Ventilation calculations are using a placeholder value rather than the actual building specification. This could cause:
- Incorrect ventilation heat transfer
- Night ventilation not working (SOLAR-04)
- All ventilation-related validation failures

## Root Cause

The `from_spec` or building assembly parsing is not extracting the ventilation airflow rate and passing it to the physics implementation.

## Suggested Approach

1. **Trace the flow**: BuildingSpecification → ThermalModelData → physics_impl.rs
2. **Find where ventilation_airflow should come from**: Check `BuildingAssembly`, `ConstructionSet`, or zone specification
3. **Implement proper extraction**: Replace the TODO with actual value from building spec
4. **Add validation**: Ensure ventilation ACH matches ASHRAE 140 case definitions

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Both TODO lines replaced with actual `ventilation_airflow` from building spec
- [ ] Case 650 night ventilation shows different energy than Case 600 (night ventilation test)
- [ ] No regression in ventilation isolation tests

issues.body:

- [ ] Integration path to main Fluxion thermal model defined

issues.title: feat(physics): Complete CAV terminal unit implementation (Issue #1903)
issues.body:
## Problem Statement

ARCHITECTURE.md mentions a `CavTerminal` trait (#1903) but only VAV terminal is implemented. CAV (Constant Air Volume) terminal units are simpler than VAV but still need implementation.

**ARCHITECTURE.md**: _"`CavTerminal` trait (#1903) — CAV terminal unit composing Fan + CoolingCoil + HeatingCoil (constant volumetric flow, Issue #1903)"_

**Currently implemented**: `VavTerminal` (#1764), `Doas` (#1765)
**Missing**: `CavTerminal`

## Evidence

- File: `src/sim/hvac/cav_terminal.rs` — trait mentioned but no implementation visible
- Issue: #1903 (referenced in ARCHITECTURE.md)

## Impact

CAV systems are common in commercial buildings. Without a CAV model:
- Cannot validate against CAV-based ASHRAE 140 cases
- HVAC BESTEST cases cannot include CAV systems
- Incomplete coverage of HVAC system types

## Suggested Approach

1. **Implement `CavTerminal` trait**:
   ```rust
   pub trait CavTerminal: Send + Sync {
       fn compute_terminal_performance(&self, control: &CavTerminalControl) -> CavTerminalPerformance;
       fn supply_air_flow(&self) -> f64;  // constant
   }
   ```

2. **Compose from existing components**:
   - FanComponent (#1761)
   - CoolingCoil (#1762)
   - HeatingCoilComponent (#1763)

3. **Add to HVAC BESTEST**:
   - Case E100: CAV heating only
   - Case E200: CAV cooling only

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `CavTerminal` trait implemented in `src/sim/hvac/cav_terminal.rs`
- [ ] Composes FanComponent + CoolingCoil + HeatingCoil
- [ ] Constant volumetric flow (no damper modulation)
- [ ] Used in at least one HVAC BESTEST case
